channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: A Major Victory for Businesses, Vapers and Public Health
item.description: The Fifth Circuit ruled that the FDA unlawfully imposed a comparative efficacy standard on flavored vaping products without the notice-and-comment process required by the Administrative Procedure Act. The standard required manufacturers to demonstrate greater benefits for adult smokers than tobacco-flavored products, contributing to widespread marketing denials. The text argues that these barriers restrict potentially lower-risk alternatives for smokers and increase healthcare costs. It also distinguishes lack of FDA authorization from proof that a product is dangerous, noting that authorization does not establish safety. The ruling calls for lawful, transparent regulation that protects young people, allows businesses fair participation, and preserves adult access to potentially beneficial alternatives to cigarettes. (Published on October 06, 2026byprotectingtaxpayers.org)

item.title: The Smoke Has Simply Become Tax-Compliant
item.description: A cigarette does not become a public health success because the tax stamp is in order. Legal sales can still mean continued exposure to smoke, disease and premature death, even while governments collect revenue from the product causing the harm. That is the uncomfortable contradiction behind tobacco control built too heavily around compliance. The goal should not be smoke that is properly taxed; it should be fewer people inhaling smoke at all. (Published on October 06, 2026bysubstack.com)
